name: Pinecone
tagline: Fully managed serverless vector database with built-in embedding, reranking and assistants.
description: Pinecone is the best-known managed vector database: you create an index, upsert vectors with metadata and query, with no clusters to size. Its serverless architecture separates storage on object storage from compute, so you pay for reads, writes and storage rather than pods, and Dedicated Read Nodes give predictable latency for heavy query loads. Pinecone also hosts embedding and reranking models (Pinecone Inference) and a RAG 'Assistant' API. It is closed source and cloud-only (with BYOC for enterprises), so you trade portability and cost control for convenience.

pricing.notes: Starter: 2 GB storage, 2M write and 1M read units/month. Standard ($50 min) and Enterprise ($500 min) are pay-as-you-go above the minimum; BYOC priced via sales.

scale.notes: Serverless indexes scale storage and query capacity automatically; namespaces support large multi-tenant workloads. Indexes live in a single region.

strengths: No infrastructure to run; indexes scale automatically
Dense and sparse vectors for hybrid retrieval
Hosted embedding and reranking models in the same API
Mature SDKs and integrations with LangChain, LlamaIndex and most RAG frameworks
weaknesses: Closed source, cloud-only outside enterprise BYOC
Read-unit pricing makes high-QPS workloads expensive
Limited query expressiveness beyond vector plus metadata filters
Plan minimums ($50/$500) add cost for small production apps
useCases: Multi-tenant AI apps with per-customer namespaces
notIdealFor: Teams needing self-hosted or open-source software
Very high QPS on a tight budget
